The RRF domain weighting primitive combines reciprocal rank fusion with domain-specific boosts to enhance retrieval accuracy. It uses parameters K=60, α=0.55, and applies domain priors such as SAME_DOMAIN_BOOST=1.6, OTHER_DOMAIN_DEMOTE=0.90, and CROSS_DOMAIN_DEMOTE=0.25. This ensures that within a search, sports-related documents receive higher scores than non-sports ones. The deduplication primitive operates on title keys to remove duplicate entries, preserving only one instance per unique title. Its failure mode arises when semantically different documents share titles, leading to false negatives. The contamination filtering primitive addresses v1 data issues by applying a minimum priority threshold, preventing outdated or low-quality records from influencing the index. These primitives form a layered architecture where each step refines the corpus quality for downstream GSI and GSE applications.
